# Release-name corpus (spec §7, architecture.md §10, FR-L2).
#
# One case per line: the filename, a TAB, and the JSON the parser must
# produce for it — title_key, episode, season, kind, group, version, with
# null where the name says nothing. Blank lines and lines starting with "#"
# are ignored. Every line is asserted by tests/test_parser_corpus.py; the
# episode+kind and title_key precisions it reports are the numbers the M5
# definition of done is measured against.
#
# The names are real release conventions from SubsPlease, Erai-raws, EMBER,
# Judas, ASW, Anime Time, HorribleSubs, Commie, Coalgirls, Kametsu, Yameii,
# MTBB, Beatrice-Raws, Nyanpasu, Doki and Zero-Raws, plus scene-style dot
# names, bare manual drops, movies, OVAs, specials, creditless files,
# batches, v2 re-releases, absolute numbering, fractional episodes,
# Japanese episode markers, dual-audio and 4K tags, and seasons written
# five ways.
#
# The expectations were written by hand and are the *specification* of the
# parser, not a snapshot of it: where the two disagreed the parser was
# changed. A handful of judgements are worth stating, because they are the
# ones a reader is most likely to question:
#
#   * A season marker is removed from the title and moved into `season`.
#     "Mob Psycho 100 II" is therefore title_key "mob psycho 100", season 2 —
#     and so is "Mob Psycho 100 2nd Season". The matcher normalises catalogue
#     titles through exactly the same function, so the two sides agree.
#   * A bare trailing number is *not* a season marker. "Chihayafuru 3",
#     "Steins;Gate 0", "86", "Hibike! Euphonium 2" and "Ghost in the Shell
#     SAC_2045" keep their numbers, because the catalogue carries them too.
#   * "Part N" becomes a season only when nothing else named one. Releases
#     use it for both "second cour" and "second season", and the second
#     reading is the one that helps a match.
#   * Punctuation is flattened to spaces in title_key, never deleted, so
#     "Re:Zero" and "Re Zero" are one key.
#   * A fractional number is a recap between two episodes, not one of
#     them. "… - 12.5" is episode 12 with kind `special` (and, in the
#     fields this file does not pin, episode_fraction 0.5), because
#     linking it as episode 12 would put a summary where the episode goes.
#   * "第3話" is episode 3 and the marker is removed from the title, for
#     the same reason a season marker is: otherwise every episode of a
#     show has a different title and none of them is the catalogue's.
#   * A *repeated* trailing exclamation mark is a season marker — the K-ON!!
#     convention. "K-On!!" is season 2 of "K-On!", and once title_key has
#     flattened the punctuation nothing else in the filename distinguishes
#     two shows with different episode counts. A single "!" is just
#     enthusiasm and is left alone ("Bocchi the Rock!").

# the parser used to get wrong — a fractional episode (12.5 is a recap
# between 12 and 13, so episode 12 and kind `special`) and the Japanese
# episode marker a raw group writes (第3話 is episode 3, and the marker
